hydraulics.note: Mains pressure at the laundry tap 52 m head static; the tank's gravity tap delivers under 1 m of head and could not run a sprinkler.

maintenance: Gutters cleaned twice, 3 hours each, both in autumn.
Compost tumbler turned weekly; about 20 minutes a week in total with feeding.

implications: The 5 kL tank on the garage roof filled only in late winter and was empty at the end of every month from November to April; the house roof, almost five times larger, is not connected.
Indoor use was close to the course convention, with toilet and laundry together about a third of it: a steady year-round demand that rainwater could serve if the client wants it to.
Air temperature fell below zero on 58 nights in the year, nearly all between May and September; anything installed outside needs frost protection or it will not meet the winter-reliability priority.
The herb strip's poor growth is explained by shade and eucalypt roots, not by soil chemistry.
questions: Whether the client would accept rainwater in the laundry if toilet flushing alone does not justify a pump.
How much of the back lawn the children actually use; the 100 m² figure is the client's, not a measurement.

hydraulics.served_now: whole house and drip, through the existing pressure pump
hydraulics.note: Existing pump cuts in at 20 m and out at 34 m of head; the drip zones run off the same pump.

maintenance: Drip emitters cleared four times, 2 hours each; two lines replaced.
Cartridge filter changed every eight weeks, $12 per cartridge.

implications: Emitter blockage is calcium carbonate scale from hard bore water, not biofilm; the fix is filtration and flushing, not new lines.
Carted water arrived in 12 loads of 12 kL, mostly between October and March. The bore allocation was fully used, evenly across months, because the bore pump tops up the tank whenever there is room.
Only one of the five guttered roof zones is connected; the other four together are about twice its area.
The tap timer gave the shade-house vegetables and fruit block about 30 per cent of the irrigation they needed; from December to February the tank was usually empty by mid-morning.
questions: Whether the bore allocation could be renewed on the same terms; the licence is reviewed in 2031.
How the family would run a composting toilet during summer heat, which the specialists did not observe.

maintenance: Pump pressure switch replaced in January, $95.

implications: The January decline in the beds is water stress compounded by salinity in the vegetable beds, not a nitrogen shortage.
The 5 kL tank on the garage roof ran dry in every month from October to April; the house roof, more than five times larger, sends all its water to the street.
The WC cistern can be supplied from outside, so toilet flushing is available to a rainwater design without opening a wall.
Existing electricity for the garden pump was small; the household's concern about running costs will turn on any new pumps, modules and consumables.
questions: What the family would accept as a manageable winter crop, which the year did not test.
Whether a salinity flush with rainwater before planting would recover the beds in one season.

hydraulics.served_now: whole house and garden, through the existing pressure pump
hydraulics.note: The floor is 3.1 m above ground. The micro-spray zone and the house share the pump, and pressure at the shower drops noticeably when the zone runs.

maintenance: Tank inlet screens cleared monthly in the wet, 30 minutes each.
Septic pumped out in November, $650, which the household had deferred.

implications: The tanks overflowed 35 kL in January and February while the household carted water in every month from May to October: a storage timing problem, not a rainfall shortage.
The west roof plane's gutter falls correctly to two downpipe positions; it can be connected without regrading.
Overflow currently scours the ground beside the piers. A test pit south-east of the shed drained a filled 300 mm hole in 55 minutes, so a dispersal point there is plausible.
The micro-spray zone and the house share one pump, and the shower pressure drop when both run is the household's most frequent complaint.
questions: Whether a neighbour could check the system during the July absence, which would change what can be left running.
How long the existing poly tanks will last; both show sun-bleaching on the north side.
